messages:
maria: quick report — brought up llama-3-7b quant-int8 across same A100 SKU in AWS/GCP/Azure (matched image + model build). seeing a consistent p95 tail on GCP that's ~2x AWS/Azure. wondering if others have seen driver/CUDA micro-behavior like this. :thinking_face:
jonathan: can you paste the quick bench numbers and the driver/cuda reported on each? simple table is fine.
ekaterina: fwiw often it's cublas/cublasLt algo choice or memcpy stall on the host path. small differences in libnvidia+kernel can flip p95.
maria: bench (single-req, seq_len=1024, beam=1, no kv reuse):
```
AWS (a100): p50 28ms, p95 62ms, throughput 18 tok/s
GCP (a100): p50 30ms, p95 123ms, throughput 15 tok/s
AZR (a100): p50 29ms, p95 68ms, throughput 17 tok/s
```

Drivers/CUDA reported from the node images: 
```
AWS: NVIDIA Driver 525.85, CUDA 12.1, libcudnn 9.4
GCP: NVIDIA Driver 525.89, CUDA 12.1, libcudnn 9.4
AZR: NVIDIA Driver 525.85, CUDA 12.1, libcudnn 9.4
```

maria: so versions look the same-ish, but GCP driver build minor rev differs (525.89) — didn't expect that to double p95. also seeing sporadic host->device memcpy stalls in the runtime logs on GCP: `hostMemcpy stalled 80ms` entries.
jonathan: do you run with the same nv-host-engine settings and power/perf governor? cloud providers sometimes default different governers. can you check `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE` and `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_driver`?
ekaterina: also verify cublasLt algo picks. add env `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` maybe, and collect `CUBLAS_LOGINFO`. small algo fallback will show in logs.
maria: quick grab from runtime logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] cublasLt: algo choose=GEMM_ALGO_14 fallback->GEMM_ALGO_3
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] kv-cache: hit
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] hostMemcpy: queued, wait=82ms
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] kernel launch: multi-head-attn fwd: 7.6ms
```

samir: @maria can you try forcing the same driver minor (525.85) on a GCP test node? I know GCP recent images pulled a patched driver that changed NVML power reporting and clock behavior.
infra-bot: automated-bench: gist://bench/1905123456 — uploaded raw traces + flamegraphs (cpu/gpu/hostmem).
maria: tried changing power management with nvml (set application clocks + disable pstate throttling) — p95 dropped from 123ms -> 70ms on the same GCP node. throughput jumped to 16 tok/s. looks like the driver + host clock interaction was part of it.
ekaterina: that matches a kernel-host-clock-power interaction I've seen. the patched driver on GCP was re-introducing a fallback path for memcpy under certain NIC interrupts.
johnathan: (typo: jonathan) small note — quant-int8 codegen also touches different cublasLt kernels than fp16; some kernels are more sensitive to memcopy latency. good catch.
maria: action items:
- run a small A/B with pinned driver 525.85 on a GCP pool (samir to provision).
- add cublasLt logging and nvprof sample for the worst requests (ekaterina + maria).
- file vendor ticket with GCP + attach flamegraphs (maria).

samir: provisioning pool now, will mirror the same AMI from AWS. ETA 2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: also flagging this in the canary rollout notes — if customers see p95 regressions after image updates we should auto-fallback to older driver variant in routing policy until validated.
ekaterina: +1 on auto-fallback. we should also add a quick host-mem latency microbench in our smoke tests for bringup.
maria: thanks all — will post bench update once pool is up and traces are uploaded. :white_check_mark:
